item.text: {"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"During the 2023 period, Sisi demonstrably appointed and empowered personnel and institutions, but the evidence supports control and mobilization more clearly than capable performance. He directly appointed judges and oversaw the justice ministry’s digitization and case-processing program; the presidency also reported the relocation of more than 100 agencies, including 30 ministries, with about 40,000 employees and workers to the New Administrative Capital (BATCH-0002-E015; BATCH-0018-E012; BATCH-0019-E001). Carnegie reports that Sisi assigned the military a widening civilian-project role because he viewed it as the most competent and loyal state agency, providing evidence of his personnel-selection rationale, though not independent proof of competence (BATCH-0009-R10-E001). Government-reported training and specialized staffing in anti-trafficking, human-rights, judicial, and regulatory functions provide limited evidence of efforts to develop or deploy specialized implementers, but training and institutional activity do not establish performance (BATCH-0008-E007; BATCH-0023-E015; BATCH-0023-E017). There is also limited evidence of subordinate disciplinary and enforcement action, including measures involving Interior Ministry personnel, recruitment-firm licence revocations, and regulatory fines, but these are government-reported or subordinate actions rather than documented presidential decisions to replace ineffective implementers (BATCH-0023-E014; BATCH-0009-R04-E005; BATCH-0002-E035). The contrary evidence is substantial: policymaking was dominated by military and intelligence agencies; judicial independence was severely restricted; military-managed projects had considerable autonomy and opaque oversight; and available evidence does not show systematic performance-based replacement or reliable monitoring of implementation quality (BATCH-0008-E001; BATCH-0011-E016; BATCH-0009-R10-E002; BATCH-0009-R10-E004). Overall, Sisi clearly selected and empowered loyal, centralized operators and some specialized personnel, but capability for assigned programs—and especially retention or replacement based on performance—remains mixed and insufficiently demonstrated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-R10-E001","BATCH-0018-E012","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0002-E015","BATCH-0008-E007","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0023-E017","BATCH-0023-E014","BATCH-0009-R04-E005","BATCH-0002-E035"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E001","BATCH-0011-E016","BATCH-0009-R10-E002","BATCH-0009-R10-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Appointments, training, institutional activity, reported case-processing rates, disciplinary measures, and licence revocations do not by themselves establish that appointees were capable performers.","The evidence does not document systematic presidential performance reviews, retention decisions, dismissals, or replacement of ineffective implementers.","Several favorable personnel and enforcement claims are government-reported or official and lack independent verification; the military’s autonomy and information restrictions limit assessment of actual performance.","The cited disciplinary and regulatory actions are attributed to subordinate ministries or agencies, not directly to presidential replacement decisions.","The military-college training evidence does not establish that the 22 courses occurred within the target period."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported conclusion that Sisi clearly selected capable implementers.","Reframed military delegation as evidence of Sisi’s belief in the military’s competence and loyalty, not independent proof of competence.","Added the omitted disciplinary, licence-revocation, and regulatory-enforcement evidence while limiting its attribution to subordinate or government-reported personnel management.","Foregrounded the distinction between loyalty, coercive reach, institutional activity, and demonstrated capability.","Preserved the period, attribution, uncertainty, and causal limits of the supplied evidence."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Obtain personnel records, appointment and dismissal histories, performance reviews, and implementation audits.","Investigate whether presidential or cabinet-level replacement decisions followed documented implementation failures.","Seek independent evidence on the performance of military-managed civilian projects and specialized regulatory or anti-trafficking bodies."]}
